area: Imaging / Framing / Guiding (screens plus the shared providers, imaging service and native camera paths behind them)

fixes.title: The "1:1 zoom" button and the "100%" readout are fit-to-window - a 4144 px frame is shown at 987 screen px (23.8%)
fixes.summary: The earlier wave fixed only the READOUT (imaging_preview_toolbar.dart:75 now prints previewDisplayScaleProvider, so fit reads ~24%). The button itself was still a no-op: ImagingViewerStateNotifier.zoom1to1 was a byte-for-byte copy of fitToWindow. Fixed the cause: zoomLevel is a multiplier on top of fit, so 1:1 is 1/fitScale. LivePreviewArea now publishes the fit scale it already computes (new previewFitScaleProvider next to previewDisplayScaleProvider), _zoom1to1/_zoomIn/_zoomOut pass it, and zoom1to1 sets 1/fitScale. Also made the clamp absolute: minZoom/maxZoom were multipliers on fit (0.25..8.0 x fit), so on this frame the maximum reachable magnification was 8*0.2339 = 1.87x actual, and on a 9576 px sensor true 1:1 sat OUTSIDE the clamp entirely - the fix would have been unreachable for exactly the operators who need it most. Bounds are now minDisplayScale/maxDisplayScale (screen px per image px) translated through fitScale, pinned so fit is always inside the range.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/imaging/imaging_preview_zoom_scale_test.dart, 2 new tests on the real ImagingScreen at 1600x900 with a 2000x1200 frame (fit = 0.4367). (1) 'the 1:1 button really shows one image pixel per screen pixel' presses the toolbar's own 1:1 callback and asserts previewDisplayScaleProvider == 1.0, that '100%' is on screen, that AnnotationOverlayWrapper.zoomLevel == 1.0, and that ImageDisplayWidget.zoomLevel * fitScale == 1.0 (i.e. the pixels really are drawn at native scale, not just the label). (2) 'the zoom ceiling is 8x actual, not 8x fit' presses Zoom in 40 times and asserts the display scale saturates at maxDisplayScale. Command: cd packages/skotiq_app && flutter test test/screens/imaging/imaging_preview_zoom_scale_test.dart -> 4/4 pass.
fixes.revert_check: Three separate severances, each run. (a) Body: replaced zoom1to1's body with the original `state = state.copyWith(zoomLevel: 1.0, panOffset: Offset.zero);` -> FAILS 'Expected: a numeric value within <0.001> of <1.0> / Actual: <0.43666666666666665>' - exactly the fit scale, i.e. the reported symptom. (b) WIRING: restored `void _zoom1to1() => _viewer.zoom1to1();` in imaging_screen_actions.dart (call site stops passing fitScale, default 1.0) -> same failure, same numbers. (c) `void _zoomIn() => _viewer.zoomIn();` -> the ceiling test FAILS 'Expected within <0.001> of <8.0> / Actual: <3.493333333333333>' = 8 * 0.4367. Restored all three -> 4/4 pass.
fixes.caveats: previewDisplayScale() lost its last caller (LivePreviewArea now multiplies fitScale by zoomLevel directly) and was deleted; previewFitScale() is still the single definition of fit. The toolbar readout half was already correct before this fix - I did not touch it.

fixes.title: Abort capture does not actually stop the exposure - the camera runs the full duration after "Exposure cancelled"
fixes.source: reports/coverage/fix4/imaging--framing--guiding.json item 2 (P1 -> corrected P2, prior_attempt: partial). The verifier corrected the root cause: this is a SIMULATOR no-op, not a real-hardware bug (real devices already reach the driver's AbortExposure).
fixes.summary: api_camera_cancel_exposure's `sim_` branch only set `camera.status.state = Idle` and logged 'Exposure cancelled' - nothing told the in-flight exposure future, which slept on to full duration and then published ExposureComplete{success:true} and stored the frame. Measured under test: a 30 s exposure cancelled at 300 ms still returned Ok after 31.6 s. The sim path now uses the SAME abort ledger the real path uses (unified_device_ops::mark_camera_exposure_aborted / exposure_abort_generation): cancel bumps the generation, the exposure loop checks it every poll, and on a mismatch takes sim_exposure_cancelled() - park the sensor, publish ExposureComplete{success:FALSE}, return Err('Exposure cancelled') - which is what the real path does after its own generation check. A second check after the loop stops a late abort from storing the frame. Two consequential fixes came with it. (a) wait_for_camera_exposure_complete (the REAL path) now takes the acquisition generation and returns the moment it moves: a driver that keeps answering 'not complete' for an exposure it has been told to stop kept that loop publishing ExposureProgress to the duration+60 s deadline, which is the 'ring keeps counting' half of the finding, at its source rather than only in the UI. (b) An aborted acquisition surfaces from the driver as a failure of the blocking cameraStartExposure call, so making the simulator honest would have started showing 'Capture failed: Exposure cancelled' on every abort - a false error banner, on real hardware too. ImagingService._capture now absorbs that failure ONLY when this service requested the cancel; every other driver error still propagates.
fixes.test: NEW Rust test native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs mod sim_exposure_tests -> 'cancelling_a_simulated_exposure_stops_it_and_stores_nothing': starts a 30 s simulated exposure, cancels it at 300 ms, asserts the call returns Err, returns in under 5 s, and that api_get_last_image finds NO frame for that device. NEW Dart test packages/skotiq_core/test/services/imaging_service_operator_abort_test.dart, 2 tests: an operator abort must complete captureImage with null and leave exposureProgressProvider idle; a driver failure nobody asked for must still throw. Commands: cd native/skotiq_native && cargo test -p skotiq_bridge --lib sim_exposure_tests -> 2/2 pass; cd packages/skotiq_core && flutter test test/services/imaging_service_operator_abort_test.dart -> 2/2 pass.
fixes.revert_check: (a) Restored the original sim cancel body (`let mut camera = get_sim_camera().write().await; camera.status.state = CameraState::Idle;` in place of the mark_camera_exposure_aborted call) -> the Rust test FAILS on 'a cancelled exposure must not report success', and the run takes 31.64 s instead of 1.4 s - the full 30 s exposure, which is the reported symptom to the second. (b) Changed `if (!_cancelRequested) rethrow;` to a bare `rethrow;` in imaging_service.dart -> 'an operator abort does not surface as a capture failure' FAILS. Both restored -> all green.
fixes.caveats: The simulated exposure notices the abort at its next poll tick, bounded by PollerPreset::Exposure's 2 s ceiling, so it is 'stops promptly', not 'stops instantly'. Real hardware is unchanged except for the progress-loop early exit; the driver-level AbortExposure it already issued is untouched.

fixes.title: Framing screen reports the wrong sensor size (1920x1080) for a camera that delivers 4144x2822
fixes.source: reports/coverage/fix4/imaging--framing--guiding.json item 1 (P1 -> corrected P2). The verifier reversed the attribution: framing_provider/support.dart faithfully uses what the camera ADVERTISES; the liar is the manual-capture generator.
fixes.summary: api/imaging.rs's simulator capture path hardcoded `full_width = 4144 / bin_x` / `full_height = 2822 / bin_y`, a second sensor that no longer existed anywhere else: SimulatedCamera::default and get_simulator_capabilities both advertise sim_frame::SIM_W x SIM_H (1920x1080), and the sequencer/autofocus path generates that. So the Framing sidebar sized its FOV box from 1920x1080 (correctly, from the advertised geometry) while the same camera handed the Imaging toolbar and every FITS a 4144x2822 frame - the box was drawn 2.16x too narrow, and no HFR/focus measurement taken through one path could be compared with one from the other. The path now reads sensor_width/sensor_height off the simulated camera's own status, so there is no second declaration left to drift.
fixes.test: NEW Rust test native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs mod sim_exposure_tests -> 'simulated_frame_matches_the_advertised_sensor': runs a simulated exposure and asserts the stored frame's (width, height) equals the (sensor_width, sensor_height) the same camera reports through its status - the invariant, not a copy of the literal. Command: cd native/skotiq_native && cargo test -p skotiq_bridge --lib sim_exposure_tests -> 2/2 pass.
fixes.revert_check: Restored `let full_width = 4144 / bin_x as u32; let full_height = 2822 / bin_y as u32;` -> FAILS 'the delivered frame must have the geometry the camera advertised / left: (4144, 2822) / right: (1920, 1080)', the exact contradiction the report screenshotted. Restored -> pass.
fixes.caveats: Simulator-only, as the verifier established: on real ASCOM/INDI hardware the delivered frame already matches CameraXSize, so no user with real gear ever got a wrong FOV box from this. The manual path still uses generate_simulated_image (random) while the sequencer path uses sim_frame (a physical electron model); unifying the two GENERATORS is a separate, larger piece of work - this closes the geometry contradiction the finding is about.

fixes.title: Framing sidebar "Equipment" section shows an indefinite spinner (residual: the churn behind it)
fixes.source: reports/coverage/fix4/imaging--framing--guiding.json item 5 (P2 -> corrected P3). The RENDERING half was already fixed in wave 3 (target_and_equipment.dart now passes skipLoadingOnReload: true on both `.when` call sites and the status badge says 'Loading…' instead of painting an empty SizedBox) - re-verified in source and by packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/framing/framing_equipment_reload_flicker_test.dart, 2/2 pass. This entry is the residual that fix explicitly left open.
fixes.summary: framingFOVProvider read exactly two fields off the camera - connectionState and deviceName - but watched the whole cameraStateProvider snapshot, so every telemetry tick (sensor temperature, cooler power, exposure progress) invalidated it and re-ran its async backend.getCameraStatus round trip. That churn is what the skipLoadingOnReload fix was covering up: the card stopped FLASHING, but the driver round-trip still fired several times a second for a number that changes only on connect/disconnect/rename. Narrowed the watch to `cameraStateProvider.select((s) => (s.connectionState, s.deviceName))`.
fixes.test: NEW packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/framing_fov_camera_churn_test.dart, 2 tests. (1) Resolves framingFOVProvider against a counted getCameraStatus, then pushes two updateTemperature ticks and two setExposing progress updates and asserts the query count is STILL 1. (2) Guards the inverse - setDisconnected must still re-run the provider and turn the card into EquipmentStatus.noCameraSpecs - so the narrowing cannot become 'the card never notices the camera was pulled'. Command: cd packages/skotiq_core && flutter test test/providers/framing_fov_camera_churn_test.dart -> 2/2 pass.
fixes.revert_check: Replaced the select with the original `final cameraState = ref.watch(cameraStateProvider);` (plus two locals so the rest of the body still compiles) -> test 1 FAILS 'Expected: <1> / Actual: <2>' - the telemetry burst re-ran the round trip. Restored -> 2/2 pass.
fixes.caveats: Riverpod's select compares the record structurally, so this is exact, not a debounce. The FOV still re-computes on profile change, framing-state change, backend swap and connect/disconnect, which is the full set of inputs it reads.

fixes.source: reports/coverage/fix4/imaging--framing--guiding.json item 3 (P2 -> corrected P3). The verifier already established the filed root cause was wrong: Dither and Stop ARE gated (guiding_panel.dart `isEnabled: isConnected && isGuiding`); the defect is that a disabled OUTLINE SmallButton was drawn identically to an enabled one.
fixes.summary: Fixed by wave 3 (reports/coverage/fixes/w3-imaging.json). Confirmed in the current source: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/imaging/widgets/panel_widgets.dart:898-906 now computes `outlineColor = isEnabled ? primary : textMuted.withValues(alpha: SkotiqTokens.opacityDisabled)`, border/icon/label share one contentColor, and the MouseRegion cursor is SystemMouseCursors.forbidden when disabled. No dither is ever silently skipped - it was already impossible to fire one.

fixes.revert_check: Not re-done: the fix and its revert-check are recorded in reports/coverage/fixes/w3-imaging.json. Re-ran the test as it stands -> green.

fixes.title: The autofocus result overlay never auto-dismisses and follows the user onto every other screen
fixes.summary: Closed since the fix4 audit ran. packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/autofocus_progress_provider.dart now carries AutofocusOverlayNotifier.resultAutoDismissDelay = 10 s: onAutofocusCompleted and onAutofocusCancelled arm a timer that calls dismiss(), onAutofocusStarted and dismiss() cancel it, and onAutofocusFailed deliberately does NOT arm it (a failure's status line is the only place the reason is written, so it stays until read). The completion path is wired: device_service/autofocus_controls.dart:347 calls onAutofocusCompleted on the real run.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/widgets/autofocus_progress_overlay_dismiss_test.dart -> 3/3 pass, asserted through the RENDERED overlay (the pill leaves the screen), not through the timer.
fixes.revert_check: Not re-done - the fix predates this wave. Re-ran the test as it stands -> green.
fixes.caveats: The overlay is still shell-mounted rather than scoped to the Imaging route, and deliberately so: it is documented as the app's single live V-curve surface and must survive a screen change DURING a run (a sequencer-driven autofocus while the operator is on the Sequencer screen). What the finding was actually about - persistent chrome sitting on unrelated screens' controls for 23 minutes AFTER the run - is what the auto-dismiss removes. The verifier also retracted the report's 'the X re-expands instead of dismissing' sub-claim.

fixes.title: FITS omits XPIXSZ/YPIXSZ (and OBJECT) although onboarding collects pixel size
fixes.summary: Fixed by an earlier wave. imaging_service/persistence.dart no longer hardcodes `pixelSizeX: null` with the stale 'not stored in profile yet' comment: it resolves the UNBINNED sensor pitch through a _sensorPixelPitchMicrons helper and passes it to FitsWriteHeader, writing each axis only when the driver reports a positive value so a one-axis driver gets one card and a 0.0 'unknown' gets none. The missing OBJECT was never a bug - persistence.dart already passes `objectName: targetName`, which is legitimately null for a manual capture with no session target, as the verifier noted.
fixes.revert_check: Not re-done - the fix predates this wave. Re-ran the test as it stands -> green.
